prompt: A tiler checks two grout lines cut by a third straight line. She finds a pair of co-interior (same-side interior) angles that BOTH measure $78^\circ$. Are the two grout lines parallel?

choices.label: No — co-interior angles would have to add to $180^\circ$, and $78 + 78 = 156$
Yes — the two angles are congruent, so the lines are parallel
Yes — any two equal angles at a transversal prove lines are parallel
There is no way to decide without measuring a third angle

hint: Which parallel-line pairs are congruent, and which one is supplementary?

hints.text: Which parallel-line pairs are congruent, and which one is supplementary?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Check an easy pair: co-interior angles of $110^\circ$ and $70^\circ$ add to $180$, so those lines ARE parallel. Run that same addition test on $78$ and $78$.
Co-interior angles are the supplementary pair. Do these two add to $180^\circ$?
$78 + 78 = 156 \ne 180$, so the lines are not parallel.

explanation: On parallel lines, co-interior angles must be supplementary, summing to $180^\circ$.
Here they sum to $78 + 78 = 156^\circ$, which is not $180^\circ$.
The condition fails, so the grout lines are not parallel — they tilt toward each other and would eventually meet.

alternativeExplanations.title: Where the missing degrees go
steps: The two interior angles fall $180 - 156 = 24^\circ$ short of a straight pairing.
Those missing $24^\circ$ are exactly the angle at which the two grout lines would eventually meet — a real problem for a tile pattern that is supposed to stay square.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap is answering "yes, they are congruent." Congruence proves parallel only for corresponding, alternate interior, or alternate exterior pairs — never for co-interior.
Before using an angle fact, name the pair first. Once you say "co-interior," the test you owe is $= 180^\circ$, and $156^\circ$ fails it.
